league.title: Firm league
league.lead: Twenty houses ranked by gross multiple.
league.measure: Gross multiple = (returned + model value of holdings) ÷ invested. Before fees. Rival firms start with the companies they already own.
league.h2h.total: {count, plural, one {# auction lost} other {# auctions lost}}
league.noDeals: No deals since the game began.
league.house.0.style: Large industrial components. Buys with discipline and walks away when it gets expensive.
league.house.2.style: Cold chain logistics specialist. Pays fair value and no more.
league.house.3.style: Sector-agnostic. The highest bidder in any auction.
league.house.4.style: Small-cap value buyer. Buys building products cheap.
league.house.5.style: Business services roll-up. Pays up for companies it can add to a platform.
league.house.6.style: Food manufacturing. Takes its time and looks for a long while.
league.house.7.style: Small-cap generalist. Shows up on any small deal.
league.house.8.style: A US house building healthcare platforms. Pays a little over the market.
league.house.9.style: German Mittelstand industrials. Checks every number and does not stretch.
league.house.10.style: Mostly succession deals at German family companies. Will look at small ones.
league.house.11.style: French business-services build-ups. Generous for companies that fit a platform.
league.house.12.style: Goes after carve-outs from large French groups. Seen only on bigger deals.
league.house.13.style: Bids hard for carve-outs from Korean conglomerates.
league.house.14.style: Smaller healthcare and services deals in Korea.
league.house.15.style: Succession buyouts of Japanese industrials. Disciplined, bids under the market.
league.house.16.style: Buys non-core subsidiaries of Japanese groups, food above all.
league.house.17.style: A Chinese growth and logistics house. Bids high in auctions.
league.house.18.style: A Chinese small and mid-cap generalist. Any sector.
